messages:
maria: Heads up — live traffic started spiking errors for the experimental /prompt-mux endpoint at 15:02 UTC. Getting alerts from synthetic checks and a handful of customer p50/p95 504 reports.

incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED — #3070123456 — prompt-mux 5xx surge (severity: P1). PagerDuty: oncall@maria. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prompt-mux

maria: I'm on it. Quick triage: is this the new routing rollout from the 14:50 deploy?

kevin: yes, that canary (deploy/2026-03-15-prompt-mux) flipped traffic yesterday ramping to 30% this morning. I saw elevated tail latency in canary logs around 14:58.

samir: customers seeing 3xx->504 chain, looks like our new handler is timing out when upstreams return large streaming responses. logs:
```
2026-03-15T15:01:59Z ERROR handler timeout after 12s: upstream read stalled
trace: prompt-mux/handler.cpp:142
```

maria: ok. If it's a handler timeout we should kill the flag and route back to stable immediately. Can someone check feature-flag state?

deploy-bot: Feature flag check: flag "ff.prompt_mux.experimental_route_v2" = on for 30% of traffic (rolloutId: r-9a4f). API: POST https://deploy.internal/flags/toggle

kevin: toggling now to off for all users. Doing a hard flip (no gradual).

kevin: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://deploy.internal/flags/toggle -d '{"flag":"ff.prompt_mux.experimental_route_v2","state":"off"}'`

kevin: done. Response: {"status":"ok","new_state":"off"} 

incident-bot: FEATURE FLAG CHANGE — ff.prompt_mux.experimental_route_v2 set to OFF by kevin at 15:06 UTC

eva: I'm watching traffic — metrics show 90% of requests already back to stable path. Error rate dropping from 4.8% -> 0.6% over the last 60s.

helena-csm: CS is getting questions from two enterprise customers in eu-west-1 about degraded responses. I posted a quick note in the customer channel; they want an ETA.

maria: short answer: rollback applied via kill-switch, investigation ongoing. ETA 30m for root cause + postmortem. Can we confirm if any persisted state was corrupted?

samir: no signs of corrupted state. Cache keys look sane. The issue seems specific to our new streaming buffer logic — large payloads block the read loop after a particular pattern. I have a repro and will open a PR to revert the change.

kevin: I'll create a rollback PR for the canary artifact to pin it to last-known-good. Also paging platform-SRE to keep an eye on infra.

maria: paging SRE (pager): @oncall-sre — can you confirm if any infra-induced backpressure contributed?

deploy-bot: PagerDuty notification sent to group oncall-sre.

oncall-sre (samir): looks purely application-level. No host OOMs or network saturation. CPU on canary nodes normal.

maria: good. Helena — please send customers the short status: "We've flipped traffic back to the stable route and are investigating root cause — service restored, no user data loss suspected. Will follow up in 60m with a technical summary." Add that we've opened a postmortem and we'll share it.

helena-csm: sending now. cc: @kevin @samir

maria: ok — handoff update: I'm going offline for an incident in 20m, kevin will take postmortem coordination. kevin — can you own timeline and follow-ups?

kevin: taking ownership for postmortem and customer follow-up. I'll collect logs, attach the failing request sample, and draft the root-cause analysis.

maria: quick checklist for the postmortem:
- timestamped timeline of deploy -> errors -> flip
- reproducible minimal repro + failing request payload
- root cause: streaming buffer regression in handler
- mitigation: feature-flag kill-switch + revert PR + unit/integration tests to cover streaming case
- impact: list of affected customers / regions (CS to confirm)

samir: opened PR #5123 to revert the streaming buffer change and added a failing unit test. CI will run, but we should not roll forward until we validate.

kevin: I'll wait for CI and then coordinate a controlled rollback to canary baseline if green. If CI fails, we'll schedule a hotfix release later today.

deploy-bot: NOTE: When re-deploying, please follow the safe roll policy: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with monitoring gates. Link: https://redwood.internal/deploys/safe-roll

helena-csm: CS updated customers: "Service restored; engineers reverted an experimental routing change. We're continuing to monitor and will share a follow-up within one hour." Customers acknowledged, two asked for incident ticket numbers — they have them now.

maria: closing the immediate P1 stopgap: feature flag off and traffic restored. Keeping this incident open for RCA — switching severity to P2 for postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigated, severity set to P2. Owner: kevin.

kevin: starting RCA doc now: https://redwood.internal/rcas/3070123456. I'll ping once draft is ready for review.

maria: thanks everyone. If anything regresses re-open thread or ping pager. :thumbsup:

kevin: handed off — taking it from here.

maria: (left channel)
